item.title: Saturday, November 21
item.description:
Good morning. Today is Saturday, November twenty-first, twenty twenty-six.

Starting with your local weather in Arkadelphia, expect mostly sunny skies today with a high near seventy-six degrees. Winds will be light out of the south-southeast at zero to five miles per hour, with just a one percent chance of rain. Tonight brings partly cloudy skies with a low around fifty-three degrees and calm winds. On Sunday, temperatures will reach seventy-three degrees in the morning before falling to around sixty-eight in the afternoon, bringing a fifty-one percent chance of rain after nine a.m. with less than a tenth of an inch expected. Sunrise is at six fifty a.m. and sunset is at five oh five p.m., with no active weather alerts.

Turning to top headlines from around the world.

Per NPR, United Nations talks in Geneva ended Saturday without reaching a legally binding agreement on autonomous weapons and military artificial intelligence. Humanitarian organizations warn that military technology is moving much faster than diplomacy, but participating nations agreed only to extend discussions for two more years.

In Los Angeles, the BBC reports that a federal jury convicted thirty-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht of arson for starting the deadly Palisades Fire in January twenty twenty-five. Prosecutors established that Rinderknecht was angry in the days leading up to the blaze, which killed twelve people and destroyed more than sixty-eight hundred buildings.

In international law enforcement, Mexican authorities arrested drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as Chapo Isidro, following a shootout in Sinaloa. Per CBS News, Meza Flores was on the FBI top ten most wanted list for drug trafficking and torture, and his capture sparked immediate violence in the area.

Back in Washington, a Senate permitting reform bill aimed at speeding up renewable energy projects has divided environmental groups, as reported by NPR. While clean energy advocates support faster approvals, many oppose provisions that aid oil and gas development. Meanwhile, the BBC reports that the FBI is investigating a potential hack of its National Crime Information Center database, which federal and local law enforcement rely on to share critical crime information.

Moving over to the gridiron for Kansas City Chiefs and NFL news.

The seven-and-two Kansas City Chiefs host the three-and-seven Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon at Arrowhead Stadium. Per Arrowhead Pride, Kansas City enters as sixteen-and-a-half-point favorites as they remain tied with the Denver Broncos atop the AFC West. The Chiefs will be without starting right tackle Jaylon Moore, who was ruled out after injuring his ankle in Week Nine. Running back Kenneth Walker the Third also remains sidelined with a groin issue.

The visiting Cardinals arrive severely depleted. Arizona lost top wide receiver Michael Wilson for the season to a neck injury and previously traded starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett. On top of that, starting quarterback Carson Beck is questionable with back spasms. If Beck cannot play, Arizona will start forty-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson, marking their fourth starting quarterback in four weeks. Following Sunday, the Chiefs begin a five-game stretch against Buffalo, the Los Angeles Rams, Cincinnati, New England, and San Francisco.

Shifting to college hoops for the Kansas Jayhawks.

In Kansas men's basketball, the eleventh-ranked Jayhawks fell to the eighth-ranked Houston Cougars in the championship game of the Players Era Eight Tournament. Per Yahoo Sports, Houston player Mercy Miller led the Cougars past Kansas to capture the title, leaving the Jayhawks with a second-place finish in the tournament. Head coach Bill Self and Kansas will now regroup as they continue their non-conference schedule.

item.title: Friday, November 20
item.description:
Good morning. Today is Friday, November twentieth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting off in Arkadelphia, you can expect sunny skies today with a high near seventy-five degrees, though temperatures will dip to around seventy this afternoon. Winds will stay light out of the east at zero to five miles per hour, with a zero percent chance of rain. Tonight brings mostly clear conditions with a low dropping to around forty-eight degrees and a one percent chance of rain. Saturday looks mostly sunny with a high near seventy-five once again. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise was at six fifty a.m. and sunset will be at five oh five p.m.

Turning to top headlines around the world. A second federal judge has stepped in to halt construction on President Trump's proposed triumphal arch. Per NPR, a federal judge in Virginia stated she will issue a preliminary injunction against the project, ruling that the initiative is unlikely to succeed in court. Her ruling goes further than a D.C. federal judge who issued a temporary block earlier this week.

In Congress, the Senate passed a bipartisan energy measure to speed up approval processes for power plants and data centers. According to NPR, lawmakers pushed the bill forward as Americans face climbing energy costs and surging electricity demand driven by artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Over in Texas, a state execution took over an hour after prison staff struggled to locate a suitable vein for inmate Reinaldo Dennes. NPR reports that Dennes moaned in pain during the procedure. On the same day, Florida carried out its twentieth execution of the year, setting a new state record.

Overseas, Polish officials reported that a Russian missile struck inside Poland while Ukraine's allies were conducting a joint military exercise. According to BBC News, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incident as a deliberate provocation from Moscow, though no injuries or damage were reported.

Moving on to football and the NFL landscape. The seven-and-two Kansas City Chiefs return to Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday to host the three-and-seven Arizona Cardinals. Per Yahoo Sports, Arizona will start forty-year-old journeyman quarterback Josh Johnson after starter Carson Beck suffered a back injury. Kansas City sits tied atop the AFC West with the Denver Broncos and trails the Buffalo Bills by one game for the top seed in the conference. On the injury front for Kansas City, starting right tackle Jaylon Moore missed practice again with an ankle injury, while running back Kenneth Walker the third is making progress with his groin issue.

Looking around the rest of the league, former Chiefs safety Justin Reid is back on the market after being released by the New Orleans Saints. Per Arrowhead Pride, Reid started nine games in New Orleans this season before being placed on waivers. In Los Angeles, Rams star receiver Puka Nacua is likely out for the remainder of the season after suffering a knee injury, according to Yahoo Sports.

Pivoting over to college basketball and the Kansas Jayhawks. The Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team suffered their first loss of the season on Thursday night, falling ninety-two to eighty-three against Houston in the championship game of the Players Era tournament in Las Vegas. Per ESPN, top freshman Tyran Stokes returned from an ankle injury to deliver a strong performance, recording twenty-two points and ten rebounds. Kansas rallied back from a heavy second-half deficit to get within four points, but Houston held on late to claim the title and bolster its case for the top spot in the national rankings.

item.title: Thursday, November 19
item.description:
Good morning. Today is Thursday, November nineteenth, 2026.

Starting out in Arkadelphia, you can look forward to a mild, pleasant afternoon under mostly sunny skies. Temperatures will reach a high near seventy-three degrees before dipping to around sixty-nine as the afternoon winds down, with calm winds out of the east at up to five miles per hour. There is zero chance of rain on the radar today. Tonight stays dry and turns partly cloudy, dropping down to a low around forty-six degrees with near-calm conditions. Looking ahead to Friday, expect plenty of sunshine with a high near seventy-four and afternoon temperatures hovering around seventy. The sun rose this morning at six forty-nine a.m. and will set this evening at five oh five p.m.

Moving to the top headlines from around the globe, President Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin have released a joint peace declaration following a historic trilateral meeting. The BBC reports that while the three leaders have previously met in one-on-one sessions, this gathering marks their first-ever trilateral discussion together.

In The Hague, the United Nations' top court has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority. The International Court of Justice determined that Myanmar security forces acted with genocidal intent during their military crackdown in northern Rakhine state back in 2017, which killed thousands and displaced hundreds of thousands more. According to the BBC, this historic verdict marks the first time an international court has ever formally found an entire state guilty of committing genocide.

Back in Washington, House Democrats have officially nominated Hakeem Jeffries to serve as the next speaker of the House, putting him on path to become the first Black speaker in American history. NPR reports that the move comes in the wake of historic midterm results where Democrats secured fifty-six percent of the national House vote compared to forty-two percent for Republicans. That fourteen-point margin represents the largest win for either party in a midterm election in fifty years, dating back to the aftermath of Watergate. Meanwhile, in Mississippi, Scott Colom has won his race to become the state's first Black United States senator in nearly one hundred and fifty years.

Over in South America, the BBC reports that Venezuela has signed a new military agreement with the United States less than a year after the removal of Nicolas Maduro. United States Secretary of Defense officials noted that Venezuela has shifted from being one of the region's sharpest threats into a compliant security partner.

Turning to the gridiron, the Kansas City Chiefs are regrouping at seven and two as they prepare to host the Arizona Cardinals at Arrowhead Stadium this Sunday. Kansas City is coming off a dominant thirty-five to thirteen road win over the Atlanta Falcons, where Patrick Mahomes regained his deep ball, throwing for three hundred forty-eight yards and five touchdowns. On the injury front, the Chiefs are taking a cautious approach with starting running back Kenneth Walker the Third, who missed the Atlanta game with a groin injury and sat out Wednesday's practice. Head coach Andy Reid told reporters that while the groin is improving, the team refuses to do anything reckless with his recovery timeline. Starting right tackle Jaylon Moore also missed Wednesday's work with an ankle injury, while tight end Travis Kelce continues to play through a lingering ankle issue that was aggravated in Atlanta. Assuming Kelce suits up Sunday, Arrowhead Pride notes it will mark his one-hundredth career regular season game at Arrowhead Stadium. item.title: Wednesday, November 18
item.description:
Good morning. Today is Wednesday, November 18th, twenty twenty-six.

In Arkadelphia, expect sunny skies today with a high near sixty-nine degrees, dropping to around sixty-four by the afternoon. Winds will be out of the east at up to five miles per hour, with a zero percent chance of rain. Tonight will be mostly clear with a low around forty degrees and calm northeast winds. Looking ahead to Thursday, it will be mostly sunny with a high near seventy-three, falling to sixty-eight in the afternoon. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise was at six forty-eight a.m. and sunset will be at five oh six p.m.

Moving on to the top headlines. House Democrats have officially nominated New York Representative Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker of the House, per NPR. The vote sets Jeffries up to become the first Black lawmaker in United States history to hold the top leadership post when Democrats assume control of the chamber in January.

Over in international affairs, President Donald Trump has arrived in Shenzhen, China, where Chinese President Xi Jinping met him directly on the tarmac, per NPR and BBC News. Trump, Xi, and Russian President Vladimir Putin are scheduled to hold a historic three-way summit on Thursday. Meanwhile, incoming House Oversight Committee Chair Robert Garcia has sent letters to thirteen Trump allies, including Donald Trump Junior, Eric Trump, Jared Kushner, and Stephen Miller, instructing them to preserve their records for upcoming congressional investigations, per NPR.

In corporate tech news, Nvidia's board of directors announced it has no plans to reinstate former chief executive officer Jensen Huang despite pressure from his allies following his recent resignation, per NPR and TechCrunch. Finally, former Democratic Representative Mary Peltola has won Alaska's highly watched Senate race, flipping the seat for her party.

Turning to the NFL, the Kansas City Chiefs delivered a commanding performance on Sunday, rolling over the Atlanta Falcons thirty-five to thirteen to improve to seven and two on the season and tie Denver for the top spot in the AFC West, per Arrowhead Pride. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes had a huge day through the air, throwing for three hundred forty-eight yards and five touchdowns, his highest single-game touchdown mark since his twenty twenty-two MVP campaign.

However, the Chiefs are monitoring a key injury, as running back Kenneth Walker missed Wednesday's practice with a groin issue, per NBC Sports. Head coach Andy Reid indicated the team will be cautious with Walker, putting him on track to miss their Week eleven matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. To shore up depth, Kansas City signed tight end John FitzPatrick and former Eagles offensive tackle Fred Johnson to their practice squad, per Arrowhead Pride. Off the field, Patrick and Brittany Mahomes shared some personal news, revealing they are expecting a baby boy, who will be their fourth child. Across the rest of the league, AP power rankings show the Buffalo Bills and Jacksonville Jaguars pulling away with firm control of their respective divisions as the second half of the season gets underway.

In college basketball, the Kansas Jayhawks men's team kicked off the Players Era Tournament in Las Vegas with a dominant performance, beating UNLV, per Rock Chalk Talk. Kansas shot sixty-two point five percent from the field, leading by twenty points at halftime and placing four starters in double figures.

The victory came at a cost, however, as top freshman Tyran Stokes went down with a knee injury early in the second half, per Yahoo Sports. Head coach Bill Self confirmed that Stokes will undergo an MRI to assess the extent of the damage. The Jayhawks remain in Las Vegas to prepare for their next tournament matchup against conference foe West Virginia.

item.title: Tuesday, November 17
item.description:
Good morning. Today is Tuesday, November seventeenth, twenty twenty-six. Let's get you moving.

Starting in Arkadelphia, you are looking at a sunny afternoon with a high near sixty-four degrees, though temperatures will fall to around fifty-eight by late afternoon. Winds will be light out of the east-northeast at zero to five miles per hour, with no rain in the forecast. Tonight will be mostly clear with a low around thirty-seven and a northeast wind near zero miles per hour. Tomorrow brings more sun and a high near seventy, dropping to sixty-five in the afternoon with light east-northeast winds. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise was at six forty-seven a.m., and sunset will be at five oh six p.m.

Now, for the top stories making news. President Trump has arrived in Manila, kicking off a three-day Asia trip that will later take him to China for historic three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump said he plans to discuss Ukraine during the trip, which contradicts what the White House previously announced. Meanwhile, Iran launched drone strikes on Tuesday against a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain, marking its third attack in recent days on American military targets in the Gulf island kingdom following a roughly two-month lull in fighting. Tehran also faces questions after a tanker was hit near the Strait of Hormuz, though officials reject any suggestion it was plotting a dirty bomb attack on Washington. The United States has officially lost its measles-elimination status after twenty-six years, as states report over five thousand four hundred cases and ten measles-related deaths this year, marking the worst numbers since the early nineteen nineties. And in Ukraine, part of the strategic Crimean Bridge partly collapsed following what President Volodymyr Zelenskyy hailed as an unprecedented missile and drone attack by Kyiv that took weeks to plan. Moscow has retaliated by targeting bridges in Kyiv, leaving residents shaken as heavy strikes hit the capital.

Turning to pro football, the Kansas City Chiefs are coming off a dominant thirty-five to thirteen blowout win over the Atlanta Falcons to improve to seven and two. Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes, rookie running back Emmett Johnson gained one hundred seventy-one yards from scrimmage in his first career start, and wide receivers Andrew Armstrong and Cyrus Allen both scored their first career touchdowns. Wide receiver Josh Downs also played his first game in a uniform for the Chiefs, who are managing a minor injury for tight end Jared Wiley as roster decisions loom. Up next, the Chiefs host the Arizona Cardinals at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, November twenty-second. Elsewhere in the league, former Chiefs wide receiver Hollywood Brown has cleared waivers and is now a free agent, while Pittsburgh Steelers reports indicate the team is eyeing a former Chiefs starting cornerback.

In college hoops, the Kansas men's basketball team begins play in the Players Era Tournament tonight with a neutral-site matchup against the UNLV Rebels, played just four miles from the UNLV campus. The Jayhawks enter the tournament climbing in the Associated Press poll following a strong start to the season, while players like Tre White begin to pull in national attention.

If you are setting your fantasy football lineup for week eleven, keep a close eye on the injury report. Key pass catchers and runners like Brock Bowers, Puka Nacua, Emeka Egbuka, Bucky Irving, Baker Mayfield, and Woody Marks are dealing with health questions ahead of Thursday Night Football. If you are scouring the waiver wire for help during a six-team bye week, quarterbacks like Jacoby Brissett and wide receivers like Jordyn Tyson are drawing attention as top pickups.

item.title: Monday, November 16
item.description:
Good morning, it is Monday, November sixteenth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting with the weather in Arkadelphia, expect sunny skies this afternoon with a high near sixty-four, though temperatures will fall to around fifty-eight later in the day. Winds will be out of the northeast around five miles per hour with a zero percent chance of rain. Tonight will be clear with a low around thirty-one and calm winds. Tuesday brings more sunshine and a high near sixty-66, dropping to around fifty-nine in the afternoon with light east-northeast winds. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise will be at six forty-six a.m. and sunset at five oh seven p.m.

Turning to the top national and international headlines, the United States is tightening controls on remote access to artificial intelligence technology. A new rule closes a loophole that allowed Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips remotely despite physical sales restrictions. Meanwhile, delegates are meeting in Geneva for United Nations talks aimed at reining in autonomous weapons, though the United States, Russia, and Israel are resisting legally binding controls, leaving campaigners fearing the window to act is closing. In domestic news, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says travel should return to normal by the end of Monday following an FAA ground stop that disrupted thousands of flights, while President Trump heads to Asia for a high-profile trilateral summit. In other news, Professor Michael Freeman told BBC Newsnight that his forensic analysis raises doubts about how Jeffrey Epstein died, stating his injuries are consistent with a homicide. Additionally, a new trial is set for the spring of twenty twenty-seven in Massachusetts for Lindsay Clancy, as prosecutors seek a criminal conviction over the killing of her three young children.

In professional football, the Kansas City Chiefs saw their legacy grow even larger in Week ten. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes threw for three hundred forty-eight yards and five touchdowns in a thirty-five to thirteen win over the Atlanta Falcons, surpassing Peyton Manning for the most career touchdown passes including the postseason with three hundred thirty-two. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson starred in his first career start while filling in for the injured Kenneth Walker, rushing for one hundred one yards and adding seventy receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns. Travis Kelce left the game early after aggravating an ankle injury, but head coach Andy Reid is managing multiple early-season scares as the seven-and-two Chiefs prepare to host the Arizona Cardinals at Arrowhead Stadium as fifteen-and-a-half-point favorites. Across the league, the Patriots expect Drake Maye to miss extended time with a serious ankle injury.

For Kansas history buffs and basketball fans, there was no new news reported for Jayhawks basketball over the past day.

For fantasy football managers navigating the Week eleven bye-week crunch, popular waiver wire targets include tight end Mike Gesicki and running backs Kaleb Johnson, Seth McGowan, and Kaelon Black. Keep a close eye on injury reports for players like Drake Maye, Kenneth Walker, and Brock Bowers as you set your lineups for the week.

Shifting to Los Angeles weather, today brings a forty percent chance of rain and a slight chance of thunderstorms before four p.m., with partly sunny skies and a high near seventy-one. Southwest winds will reach ten miles per hour. Tonight carries a thirty percent chance of rain and thunderstorms before four a.m., partly cloudy skies, and a low around fifty-three with west-northwest winds around ten miles per hour. Tuesday will be sunny with a high near sixty-eight and west-northwest winds around ten miles per hour. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise is at six twenty-six a.m. and sunset at four forty-eight p.m.

item.title: Sunday, November 15
item.description:
Good morning. Today is Sunday, November fifteenth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting in Arkadelphia, expect mostly cloudy skies today with a high near fifty-six degrees. East winds will stay light at zero to five miles per hour, and your rain chance sits at just six percent. Tonight remains mostly cloudy with a low around thirty-six degrees, near-calm northeast winds, and a slight thirteen percent chance of showers. Monday turns sunny with a high near sixty-three degrees that settles down to around fifty-nine in the afternoon, along with zero chance of rain. There are no active weather alerts in the area. Sunrise was at six forty-five this morning, and sunset will be at five oh eight this evening.

Turning to the top headlines, federal officials are dealing with the fallout from Friday's nationwide aviation ground stop that grounded thousands of flights and delayed college football games across the country. Per NPR, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed a contractor maintenance project that overloaded old copper wire equipment during an upgrade. Duffy stated the shutdown was not a cyberattack, and NBC News reports he told reporters he does not apologize for halting flights to protect travelers.

In politics, NPR reports midterm voters ended long-running Republican control in several state legislatures. Democrats took over previously divided chambers and weakened Republican dominance in others, with newly empowered state lawmakers preparing agendas focused on expanding healthcare access and limiting taxpayer-funded school vouchers.

In public health, global health authorities at the Pan American Health Organization say the United States has officially lost its measles elimination status following persistent domestic outbreaks.

In Washington, a federal judge has issued a two-week order temporarily blocking plans to redevelop the historic East Potomac public golf links near the White House into a championship course.

And in Florida, the city of Delray Beach has canceled its annual St. Patrick's Day parade after a nearly sixty-year run, citing a new state law that prohibits taxpayer funds from going toward diversity initiatives.

Out on the field, the six and two Kansas City Chiefs play the three and six Atlanta Falcons at noon on CBS. Kansas City is coming off a thirty-five to twelve blowout against the New York Jets, while Atlanta is resetting after trading away starting safety Jessie Bates and starting center Ryan Neuzil. Patrick Mahomes had an injury scare last week when he landed hard on his throwing arm, prompting the Chiefs to consult Major League Baseball doctors about his elbow, but Mahomes did not miss a snap and will play. Kansas City will be without running back Kenneth Walker, who was ruled out after waking up Friday with a tight groin. Defensive tackle Chris Jones missed team travel for personal reasons and is arriving on his own with no game designation. To add depth, the Chiefs elevated running back Nate Carter and wide receiver Jacob De Jesus from the practice squad, while newly traded wide receiver Josh Downs, acquired from the Indianapolis Colts, is expected to make his team debut wearing number twelve.

Across the league, international action in Munich brought bad news on a single snap. ESPN reports New England Patriots rookie quarterback Drake Maye and Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson were both injured on the very same play, knocking both stars out of the game and sending both sidelines into a panic.

Checking in on Kansas men's basketball, there is no real news to report for the Jayhawks today as the team is between games.
